title: Taming Latency-Memory Trade-Off in MoE-Based LLM Serving via Fine-Grained Expert Offloading
technique: FineMoE: fine-grained expert maps (iteration-level gate probabilities) plus prompt semantic embeddings to guide expert prefetching, caching and offloading between CPU and GPU memory

optimized_metrics.evidence: We aim to achieve both low memory footprint and inference latency by proposing fine-grained expert offloading.
We aim to achieve both low memory footprint and inference latency by proposing fine-grained expert offloading.
The objective is to minimize the on-demand loading latency (ideally T = 0 with perfect predictions) while limiting the total memory footprint of cached experts to satisfy the available GPU memory M.
We opt for lossless serving to design FineMoE because this line of methods avoids modifying models, hence assuring generation quality.
We should minimize expert miss and mitigate mispredictions in expert offloading.

headline_claim.text: FineMoE reduces inference latency by 47% and improves expert hit rate by 39% over state-of-the-art solutions.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 11 CDF of end-to-end request latency (online)
expert cache budget sweeps and Expert Map Store overhead (§6.7)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) is commonly employed, which measures the latency from receiving the user request until generating the first answer token.
metric_definitions.notes: Described as the prefill-stage metric; measured from request receipt (would include any queueing).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Tokens-Per-Second (TPS) or Time-Per-Output-Token (TPOT) is used to measure the generation rate of LLM serving.
metric_definitions.notes: Used for decode stage; no formula given.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: an expert hit: the activated expert is already in GPU memory (otherwise on-demand loading from CPU)
metric_definitions.notes: Paraphrase; paper's text: experts present in GPU memory (defined as an expert hit). Otherwise miss.

load_regime: Offline serving (expert map store full) at small batch (default), batch sweep 1-8 on Mixtral-8x7B; online serving with 256 requests from Azure LLM inference traces at 2.91 req/s; expert cache limit sweep 6-96 GB
tradeoff_acknowledged: The title trade-off: baselines achieve low latency with large memory footprint (e.g. no offload / ProMoE) or low memory with high latency (DeepSpeed, MoE-Infinity); FineMoE targets the Pareto point. Prefetch distance trades hit rate vs. overhead.
hardware: Six NVIDIA RTX 3090 24GB GPUs (NVLink pairs), 32-core CPU, 480 GB RAM
workloads: LMSYS-Chat-1M, ShareGPT prompts; Azure LLM inference traces for online
extractor_notes: 'Inference latency' headline = TTFT and TPOT reduction (avg across baselines); memory is a constraint via cache budget. Expert hit rate is the intermediate proxy objective. Speeds measured at small batch (batch 1 default), and online at low rate 2.91 req/s; no tail percentiles reported (CDF only). Lossless (no accuracy numbers).
load_class_quote: Offline serving with the Expert Map Store in full capacity at small batch (§6.2, batch sweep 1-8) plus online serving: "randomly sampled 256 requests (2.91 requests per second)" from Azure traces (§6.3) = offline-batch + online-arrivals
